newsitem.title: USA: U.S. energy futures firm after-hours on API data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. energy futures firm after-hours on API data.

text.p: U.S. energy futures got a lift after-hours on Tuesday as weekly stock data from the American Petroleum Institute showed a modest distillate build and unexpected draws in crude oil, traders said.
"The APIs said crude was down two million barrels but it was expected up," one ACCESS after-hours trader said.

The market was continuing to recover from lows caused by a news report late on Monday that claimed the U.S. had asked Saudi Arabia to increase crude production in the wake of Iraq's suspended exports, according to the trader.
Meanwhile, stocks of distillate rose just 235,000 barrels to 112 million barrels, or 21.5 million less than the same period last year.
NYMEX October crude oil futures traded around $23.50 a barrel in early ACCESS trade, up about 19 cents from the settle on 1,000 lots.
October heating oil futures traded 66.39 cents a gallon, 80 points higher on the relatively low distillate inventories.
Front-month gasoline futures edged up 0.46 cent a gallon to 63.20 cents on 30 lots traded.
